item.content:encoded:
In case you’re not aware, Hawaii is the 50th state of the United States. Some people often forget this, caught up in the massiveness of the ‘mainland’; making visits to places such as Hawaii with romanticized views of easy-living/vacation-getaway/day-time nap business.

This is why we’re lucky to have publications such as Contrast Magazine, who believe that “the natural allure of Hawaii attracts many diverse people, making these islands an international breeding ground for modern culture.” Publishing content that explores art, design, culture, and music, Co-Founder & pro-surfer Jason Shibata shot this video on the South Shore of Oahu using the GoProHD camera with ‘HI-808′ as the track.  Crazy image quality – check the video (below) as Jason catches some tubes.

We’re also featured in the latest Travel issue – Contrast 003: Goin’ Places.  Look for a copy or request it from your neighborhood newsstand.

Shout outs to our North F@$!in’ Shore homie Zen who expands our minds regularly, and all the In4mants crew once again.  Miss you guys!

item.dc:creator: bluescholars
item.description: Two pre-show missions: 1. Stop by the Adidas store and 2. Hit thrift shops on Hawthorne. On the first mission, we got a tour from the marketing homie from Seattle, Mark Shin. We got a glimpse of some upcoming releases, tried on Dwight Howard’s shoes, and tried to get a sponsorship for Macklemore’s homie Raven Bowie [...]
item.content:encoded:
Two pre-show missions: 1. Stop by the Adidas store and 2. Hit thrift shops on Hawthorne.

On the first mission, we got a tour from the marketing homie from Seattle, Mark Shin. We got a glimpse of some upcoming releases, tried on Dwight Howard’s shoes, and tried to get a sponsorship for Macklemore’s homie Raven Bowie for these shoes.

On the second mission, we hit up a vintage store and engaged in the time honored masculine tradition of taking pictures together in an old-school photo booth.

As for the show, I gotta say that it was the most athletic crowd we’ve ever played for in Portland. Several medicinal brownies were thrown onstage and it all ended with 1/4 of the crowd taking the party onstage.

Big thanks to Taylor Lemons for sending a few mobile phone shots  (not bad, we can almost feel the condensation on that lens), and to Adam Bussing.  He said, “We wanted to give you our special cupcakes, but we couldn’t bring them into the show without messing up our (expertly) hand-crafted frosting design…. So we brought brownies instead.” Were those your brownies thrown onstage?

Photos 2-5 are from Taylor Lemons, and medicinal cupcake photo is courtesy of Adam Bussing.  See you again real soon, Portland!

item.content:encoded:
Hari (left) and his brother Ashok (right) in 1987.

Blue Scholars and Hari Kondabolu go back. Way back. Back before time. Back before Massline Media formed in ‘06, when gas price medians rose to $4.06. He did a short film with Zia called Manoj. The Indian dude you used to see at all the shows. Before he moved to London for a minute, we met in Queens to visit to find the best Dosas in it. And then he moved back home to NYC, he rocked Blue Scholars shirts on late night TV. And we’re pleased to say, the day after today, our dude is making moves in a major way. When you see him at Comix, remember that’s my brother! Rocking a headlining set with Black Dynamite’s brother, better known to all as Baron Vaughn. So go get your tickets at www.comixny.com. Early!

item.content:encoded:
We’ve played WOW Hall in Eugene a few times now, and each time back has been hotter, sweatier, and smokier than the last. I’ve been telling the homies for a long time how crazy these kids are but, even then, Friday was unexpectedly rambunctious.

Eugene was on one. Especially for an all-ages show stacked with four DJ/MC combinations and no hypemen. Grynch, Bambu & Macklemore (and their respective DJs Nphared, Phatrick & Ryan Lewis) all killed their sets, and got their crowdsurf in during our “North By Northwest” encore. Shoutout to the young homie Marc Mercado who did some live painting during the show and gave Grynch this painting, which he will supposedly understand if and when he ever decides to drop some acid.

Thanks, Eugene. You really know how to make us feel at home. Check the photos from Sukoski Photography, below.

item.title: NEW MUSIC: New People (Empire Way Remix)
item.dc:creator: Sabzi
item.description: Geo and I listen to a whole lot of music. Some of it is dope music people think is garbage, some of it is garbage that people think is dope music, some of it is simply garbage, and occasionally, some of it is Garbage. Back in 2008, one of the tunes that was in (figurative) rotation [...]
item.content:encoded:
Geo and I listen to a whole lot of music.  Some of it is dope music people think is garbage, some of it is garbage that people think is dope music, some of it is simply garbage, and occasionally, some of it is Garbage.

Back in 2008, one of the tunes that was in (figurative) rotation on the iPhone was a little Australian hit called “Walking On A Dream” by a group called Empire Of The Sun.  Whether or not that song is garbage is up to you.  Either way, I snatched the best loops in that song, added some extra percussion, and chopped a Biggie sample for the bridge and we came up with what is now known as New People.

Since we wanted to release New People on the OOF! EP we ended up making a different version of it because a) the Empire version didn’t match the sonic texture of OOF!, and b) you can’t really do an official release of a song with such a recognizable sample anyway.  You know, lawyers and such.

Long story short, this “remix” (aka original version) didn’t come out until a year later in August ‘09 and even then I don’t remember exactly how we put it out.  We were so busy with the release of the actual EP and the Hawaii trip that I must have overlooked the fact that this remix only made it onto some crappy jewel-cased promo CD sampler that nobody listened to.  ‘Cause seriously, who the hell listens to CDs?  Every time I’m at an event and somebody gives me a demo or sampler on CD it’s like they’re saying, “Hey man, will YOU throw this away for me?”  (RIP Mitch Hedburg).

Anyway, I guess we waited too long on making this version known ’cause after the shows this weekend I was getting Twitter questions about this song from people like they never heard it before.  What’s likely more of a kick-in-the-hip-hop-testes is that, although we made this joint a year and a half ago, Wiz Khalifa has his own version that came out sometime (I think) in the last 6 months.  This of course helped make an awkward moment at the show we did with Wiz Khalifa the other day when we rocked the New People {Empire Way Remix} in front of some of his fans.

Blah blah blah blah blah, nobody cares about your apologetic late-pass rants, Saba.  Shut up and gimme the download already.

No problem, friend.  Here you go. – Sabzi

item.title: Grynch: A Reintroduction by Geo
item.dc:creator: Geo
item.description: A few years back, Sabzi and I submitted an unreleased track “Final Call” to the Reigncraft compilation series, which showcased local artists. When the CD was released, we bumped it out of curiosity and one of the tracks that stood out was by some dude named Grynch. Just as we were listening, thinking to ourselves, [...]
item.content:encoded:
A few years back, Sabzi and I submitted an unreleased track “Final Call” to the Reigncraft compilation series, which showcased local artists. When the CD was released, we bumped it out of curiosity and one of the tracks that stood out was by some dude named Grynch. Just as we were listening, thinking to ourselves, “yo, who is this dude? he can rap,” Saba goes, “yo rewind that, I think he said your name.” So I rewound it, and, it turned out we misheard it–he was just spelling “God.” 30 seconds later, Saba goes, “yo rewind that, I think he really said your name.” Yeah whatever, I thought, and reluctantly rewound it. Saba was right, dude shouted me out with the line “Geo said it best, hip-hop’s malnourished and underfed.”

Grynch – That’s Hip-hop

In rapper circles, the unsolicited shoutout is one of the highest compliments one can give another. It turned out that we and this Grynch character had mutual friends, including the homie Chris G. who gave us a copy of “This Is What I Do,” which we bumped on the ride back home from a show at Washington State University. So when Grynch hit me up to spit a verse on a remix for that very track I first heard him on (”That’s Hip-hop”), I was like sure, why not? Besides, I didn’t want to make the same mistake Saba did in previous calab holler encounters. We all cramped into Macklemore’s crib one afternoon to record the track. It took me a good minute to actually believe that the voice I heard on record belonged to this guy.

Grynch feat. Geo – Summertime

Months later, he apologized profusely for the track having never been released. Now, you’d think lil’ homie would’ve taken the L and eased up off the “calabs.” But being the young fearless Jedi that he is, he asked if I’d be down to spit on another track! That’s how “Summertime” came about. Then, dude did the impossible: he became the first local emcee not named Geo, RA Scion or Gabriel Teodros to snag a beat from Sabzi with the 2007 internet-only track “The Life I Chose,” which also has the dubious honor of being the soundtrack music for a fight that broke out during soundcheck one day long ago.

Grynch – The Life I Chose (prod. Sabzi)

Since then, we’ve toasted drinks at many bars from here to San Francisco to Hawaii, discussed the intricacies of obscure ’90s gangsta rap, and recorded a couple more songs together (”I’m a Dreamer” and “Smoke & Mirrors”). Constantly grinding out quality performances, releases and press, he’s become a town celebrity. True story: we’ll stand next to each other at shows and kids wearing Blue Scholars t-shirts will walk right past me to say wassup to him.

Grynch feat. Geo & Thig Natural – I’m A Dreamer

Grynch feat. Tunji & Geo – Smoke & Mirrors

Most recently, I was on a good one at my own birthday party and apparently tried to shove homeboy into a closet. To make amends, I’ve invited the homie along with us this Friday to play his VERY FIRST SHOW in Eugene, Oregon. So, to all Eugenians: get his music (if you haven’t yet), come through, and welcome him to his first, but certainly not last, appearance in your magical town. Maybe we’ll even run into this local metal band out there and have an epic rap-rock battle for Grynchian name-supremacy.

Download Grynch’s music at GetGrynch.com

item.title: Blue Scholars Weekend: DOUBLE FEATURE x Encore Show Recap
item.dc:creator: bluescholars
item.description: Seattle: First off, thank you for your energy, spirit and support during such an epic weekend of Blue Scholars shows. The DOUBLE FEATURE sold-out shows on Friday & Saturday proved to be an evening of audio visual treats – DV One gave us a signature mix of goodies as he dug in the YouTube crates [...]
item.content:encoded:
Seattle: First off, thank you for your energy, spirit and support during such an epic weekend of Blue Scholars shows.  The DOUBLE FEATURE sold-out shows on Friday & Saturday proved to be an evening of audio visual treats – DV One gave us a signature mix of goodies as he dug in the YouTube crates (Soul Train clips!), and we premiered our visual accompaniment to classic, new and remixed tracks.  We’re going to publish a list of the movies we remixed, so If you’re interested in checking any of them out,  stay posted.

Sunday’s Encore Show was truly an encore – we brought back Macklemore, Bambu, Gordon Voidwell and added Vitamin D & DJ Soul One to the bill to complete a weekend that was – in short – filled with momentum that’s carrying us all way into this weekend’s shows in Eugene & Portland (did you get tickets yet?).

Maybe the photos will bring you back to last weekend, or maybe they will prepare you for our upcoming shows.  Whatever the case may be, trust this: the photos below are just a glimpse of the energy that was felt in the crowd and throughout the entire 3 day marathon.  Thanks again, Seattle, and enjoy!  Courtesy of http://www.jkoephoto.com/
